messages:

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Per-tenant audit export for FinAxis — quick prioritization ask

Folks,

FinAxis (Elena and Samir, cc'd) are at contract signature; legal has one hard requirement: a per-tenant audit export that lets them pull a tenant-scoped CSV of activity and retention metadata for audits. Their procurement team has made this a gating item for go-live.

Attached is the latest requirements doc from Elena + our MAP (MAP_FinAxis_May2027.pdf). TL;DR:
- MVP needed: scheduled export (daily) per-tenant to an S3 bucket with tenant ID, event timestamp, operation type, and metadata fields they list.
- Longer-term: UI to trigger exports + retention policy controls.

As CS/Sales I need a clear ask for Product/Eng: what is the minimum scope we can commit to within 4 weeks to unblock the signature? If we cannot commit to code in that window, we need an approved manual/ops fallback (redwood-run export, signed SLA).

Questions for you:
1) Can Eng scope an MVP (scheduled S3 export) and give a rough ETA and risk list?
2) Is there any security/KMS or compliance blocker for exporting tenant-scoped audit rows?
3) If we ship an MVP, what are the perf/infra costs we should surface to the customer in advance?

Ben/Marissa — I'm looped in for the commercial implications; if Product can commit to an engineering sprint + staging rollout, we can push to sign this week.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Per-tenant audit export for FinAxis — quick prioritization ask

Thanks Grace — good context and the MAP helps.

High level reaction / next steps from Product:
- Option A (fast MVP): scheduled export job that pulls tenant-scoped audit events from the existing logging/streaming pipeline and writes gzipped CSVs to a customer-owned S3 (or a signed URL destination). Minimal UI: config as code (MAP signoff) + access controls. Estimated scope: 3–4 sprint-days (1 backend engineer + 0.5 infra) for a narrow column set.
- Option B (productized): per-tenant export UX, retention controls, audit viewer and RBAC — multi-sprint, higher QA and security review.

Questions for Eng (Dev): can you confirm the effort and call out blockers (KMS/PII masking, retention deletion workflows)? If Option A is feasible, I propose we offer that as the commercially binding MVP and schedule Option B for a later milestone.

If we do A, we should also offer an interim manual export service (ops-run) for a 2-week window to get them across the contract signature.

Markus
Markus Klein
VP Product, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:28:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Per-tenant audit export for FinAxis — quick prioritization ask

Markus/Grace — quick engineering breakdown. I attached a short tech note (eng_estimate_per_tenant_export.md). Summary:

Scope (Option A MVP):
- Hook an export job into the existing audit log stream (Kafka -> batch job) to filter by tenant ID, serialize to CSV with agreed columns, encrypt with customer KMS key, and push to an external S3 location.
- Add a scheduled job runner + small config table (tenantID -> destination + lastExport).
- Add basic validation and a single acceptance test.

Estimates & risks:
- Implementation: ~5 engineer-days (1 BE, 1 infra) to a staging demo; full QA + security review adds 3–5 days.
- KMS: we can use customer-provided KMS keys but need a key policy review — SOC/compliance will require us to validate access.
- Data volume: if FinAxis enables verbose logging per tenant, export size could spike; need S3 cost estimate and optional sampling.
- Rollout: staged — one tenant in staging, then pilot with FinAxis sandbox, then prod.

Workarounds:
- Manual ops export: we can run an adhoc job and provide files for the customer for the immediate 1–2 week window to allow signature. Ops will charge a one-time service fee.

If Product signs off, I can carve out a short spike tomorrow to get the pipeline hook in and share a demo by EOW.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: eng_estimate_per_tenant_export.md

Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 14:40:00 +0100
Subject: Fwd: Per-tenant audit export for FinAxis — roadmap ask & temporary fallback

Elena / Samir — looping back with our internal plan (thread below). Short version:

1) We can commit to Option A (scheduled per-tenant export to your S3) as an MVP. Eng estimates a staging demo by EOW and a production pilot within ~2 weeks post-security signoff.
2) If you need files immediately to satisfy procurement, we will provide a manual export (ops-run) within 48 hours for the immediate signature window; this is a one-time deliverable while Eng completes the MVP.
3) Action items for FinAxis: confirm the exact CSV schema from the attached requirements and confirm the destination S3 + KMS key details by EOD tomorrow.

We understand legal still needs to sign; if your legal team confirms the above approach (manual export + MVP roadmap) we'll mark the gating requirement satisfied and proceed with the signature.

Thanks — looking forward to the sign-off.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
